newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. council concerned at Israeli settlement plans.
newsitem.headline: U.N. council concerned at Israeli settlement plans.

text.p: The Security Council expressed concern on Tuesday over Israel's settlement policy in East Jerusalem and urged restraint so as not to undo the Middle East peace process, council president Njuguna Mahugu of Kenya said.

Speaking to reporters after council consultations on a number of topics, he also said he had been asked to call in Israel's U.N. representative to convey that concern and to ask how Israel intended to proceed.
Mahugu was referring particularly to a plan by Israel to build 6,500 homes on a hill of pine trees between Jerusalem and Bethlehem, called Har Homa by Israel and Jabal Abu-Ghneim by the Palestinians.
"The council...expressed concern at the new settlements policy of Israel in East Jerusalem and hoped that restraint and wisdom would prevail so as not to undo the peace process," he said.
"I was requested to invite the permanent representative of Israel to convey this concern and solicit his views on how Israel intends to proceed," he added.

Mahugu's statement was a follow-up to identical letters which the Arab group sent to him and to Secretary-General Kofi Annan complaining about Israel's settlement activities, particularly in East Jerusalem, and urging the council to get Israel to desist.

The letter, signed by the Palestine Liberation's U.N. observer, Nasser al-Kidwa, in his capacity as current chairman of the Arab group, referred to the "policies and illegal measures taken in occupied East Jerusalem, aimed at Judaizing the city and changing its legal status and demographic composition."

It said the Israeli authorities had confirmed their decision to build a new settlement in the Jabal Abu Ghneim region, following earlier decisions to build in the Ras al-Amud district and to keep open an archaeological tunnel near Moslem holy sites in East Jerusalem.

"Furthermore, Israel is continuing to deprive the Palestinian inhabitants of Jerusalem, who are the original inhabitants of the city, of their 'right of residence,' in the context of what appears to be an underhand campaign aimed at driving the Palestinian Arab inhabitants out of Jerusalem."

Al-Kidwa said the international community, including the Security Council, had taken a "very firm attitude towards the above-mentioned policies and actions, which it has described as null and void," and had called on Israel to put an end to them.

"The group of Arab states members of the United Nations wishes to insist on the vital importance of the issue, and requests the Security Council to take the necessary steps to induce Israel, the occupying power, to put an end to its policies and actions, and in particular definitively to renounce any settlement activity, particularly in the Jabal Abu Ghneim and Ras al-Amud region."
The Arab group letter said that "any failure in this area risks having serious consequences and disastrous sequels."
